v.checked: Re-read arXiv:1902.04655v2 (EPJC 79 (2019) 639) cold from the full 63-page PDF (downloaded via proxy). SOURCE/LOCATOR fully CONFIRMED: title, ref, 13 TeV, 2015-2016 data (37.1 fb^-1), dedicated electron reco/ID paper, Run 2. Figure 4 caption (PDF p.16): "Reconstruction efficiencies relative to reconstructed clusters, e_reco ... as a function of eta in four illustrative ET bins: 15-20 (top left), 25-30 (top right), 40-45 (bottom left), 80-150 GeV (bottom right)" -- matches extraction exactly. Figure 4 Y-axis range is 0.96-1.02 (ratio panel 0.96-1.04). Figure 2 caption (p.12): "Top: total reconstruction efficiency for simulated electrons ... as a function of true (generator) ET for each step ... As the cluster reconstruction requires uncalibrated cluster seeds with ET>2.5 GeV, the total reconstruction efficiency is less than 60% below 4.5 GeV (dashed line). Bottom: reconstruction efficiency relative to reconstructed clusters, e_reco, as a function of ET for Z->ee" -- matches. TEXT CONFIRMED: seed-cluster eff "ranges from 65% at ET=4.5 GeV, to 96% at ET=7 GeV, to more than 99% above ET=15 GeV" (p.11); "Above ET=15 GeV, the efficiency to reconstruct an electron having a track of good quality ... varies from approximately 97% to 99%" (p.14); precision/acceptance region |eta|<2.47 confirmed; crack 1.37<|eta|<1.52 confirmed; seed sliding-window 3x5 towers with summed ET>2.5 GeV confirmed (p.10); "Below ET=15 GeV, the reconstruction efficiency is determined solely from simulation; a 2% (5%) uncertainty is assigned in the barrel (endcap) region" confirmed (p.15); "uncertainty in efficiency in data is typically 1% in the ET=15-20 GeV bin and reaches the per-mille level at higher ET" confirmed. High-ET central values (0.975-0.990) all lie within the 97-99% text band and the 0.96-1.02 Fig.4 axis. Low-ET bins (3-15 GeV) match the seed-cluster/total turn-on numbers (65% at 4.5, 96% at 7, >99% at 15; <60% below 4.5).
v.corrections: (1) REPRESENTATION MISLABEL at low ET: the pt 3-15 GeV bins are read from Figure 2 TOP, which is the TOTAL reconstruction efficiency (EMclus x e_reco), NOT e_reco "relative to reconstructed clusters." This is acceptable for a Delphes total-reco card, but the bin notes citing "e_reco" / "epsilon_reco data points" for the turn-on region are technically wrong -- those are total-efficiency reads. The high-ET bins (>15 GeV) correctly use e_reco from Fig.4. (2) HIGH-ET PER-ETA FINE STRUCTURE UNVERIFIABLE: the paper tabulates no per-eta e_reco values; text only states "approximately 97% to 99%" above 15 GeV. The specific dips claimed (0.975 at the 1.37-1.52 crack, 0.975 at 1.81-2.01, 0.987 at 1.0-1.37) are eyeball reads of a plot with a compressed 0.96-1.02 axis and cannot be confirmed point-by-point; they are within band and plausible, but should not be presented as precise. (3) UNCERTAINTY for the 15-20 GeV region: paper says data uncertainty is "typically 1%" in the ET=15-20 GeV bin; the extraction's unc_rel=0.005 for the high-ET barrel bins is on the optimistic side for the lowest measured bin (per-mille only applies at higher ET). (4) The note on the 1.37-1.52 bin stating ATLAS "excludes" this region implies a forced efficiency drop; in fact e_reco is measured across the full |eta|<2.47 -- the 1.37-1.52 exclusion is an analysis-level probe selection, not an efficiency suppression (value 0.975 is fine, framing is misleading). (5) The deep-turn-on bin uncertainties (unc_rel 0.04-0.30 for pt<10 GeV) are extrapolations beyond the paper's quoted 2%/5% simulation uncertainty -- conservative and acceptable, but not sourced from the paper. None of these change the bin central values materially; all values are consistent with the figures and quoted text bands.

v.checked: I extracted the full text of the cited source arXiv:1704.07983 (= ATLAS PERF-2015-10, "Performance of the ATLAS Track Reconstruction Algorithms in Dense Environments in LHC Run 2") from the official PDF and read every figure caption. CONFIRMED the paper has exactly 17 figures (Fig 1-17). The cited "figaux_11a / Figure 11" does NOT show pT resolution vs eta: Figure 11's actual caption is "The reconstructable efficiency, defined as the efficiency to reconstruct all of the charged decay products [of the rho and three-prong tau]..." — an EFFICIENCY plot, not a resolution plot. No figure in the paper plots sigma(pT)/pT vs |eta|; the figures cover merged/shared cluster counts (Figs 4-7), charged-particle separation (Figs 8-9), reconstruction efficiency (Figs 10-14), and dE/dx / lost-track fraction (Figs 15-17). A full-text search for "momentum resolution", "sigma(pT)", "q/pT", "0.05%", and "pt resolution" returned ZERO hits — the paper presents no track-momentum-resolution formula or measurement whatsoever. Separately confirmed the base formula is internally inconsistent: claimed a=0.013 (=1.3%, not the cited 1%) and b=3.6e-4 (=0.036%/GeV, not the cited 0.05%), so the (a,b) do not derive from the quoted "0.05% x pT (+) 1%" formula. Also confirmed via the official Delphes repo that the standard ATLAS card uses entirely different charged-hadron resolution values (3 eta bins: sqrt(0.06^2+(1.3e-3*pt)^2), sqrt(0.10^2+(1.7e-3*pt)^2), sqrt(0.25^2+(3.1e-3*pt)^2)), bearing no resemblance to the extracted numbers.
v.corrections: DEDICATED FIGURE FALSE: figaux_11a / Figure 11 of PERF-2015-10 is a reconstructable-EFFICIENCY plot for rho/3-prong-tau decays, not an "expected sigma(pT)/pT vs |eta|" plot. No such resolution-vs-eta figure exists anywhere in arXiv:1704.07983. LOCATOR FABRICATED: the paper contains no momentum-resolution parametrization, no "0.05% x pT (+) 1%" formula, and no etashape normalization numbers ("4.16 vs 1.73 in figaux_11a units" are invented). SOURCE MISMATCH: the cited Run-2 dense-environment tracking paper does not support any of the extracted resolution content. BASE VALUES INCONSISTENT: a=0.013 implies a 1.3% constant term (not 1%) and b=3.6e-4 implies 0.036%/GeV (not 0.05%); the (a,b) pair is not derivable from the quoted formula. ETA BINS / SHAPE MULTIPLIERS (1.00/1.10/1.30/1.80/2.40) and PER-BIN UNCERTAINTIES (0.05/0.06/0.07/0.09/0.10) are unsupported by any cited figure and appear reverse-engineered. The actual Delphes ATLAS card charged-hadron resolution uses 3 bins with values sqrt(0.06^2+(1.3e-3*pt)^2)/sqrt(0.10^2+(1.7e-3*pt)^2)/sqrt(0.25^2+(3.1e-3*pt)^2), wholly different from the extracted fragment. The entire block's central values, uncertainties, source attribution, and locator are unverifiable against the cited source and must be discarded.

  # sigma_E/E = sqrt( (a/sqrt(E))^2 + (b/E)^2 + c(eta)^2 ),  E = pt*cosh(eta) [GeV].

    (abs(eta) <= 0.6)                    * sqrt( 0.10^2/(pt*cosh(eta)) + 0.35^2/(pt*cosh(eta))^2 + 0.010^2 ) +
    (abs(eta) > 0.6 && abs(eta) <= 1.0)  * sqrt( 0.10^2/(pt*cosh(eta)) + 0.35^2/(pt*cosh(eta))^2 + 0.010^2 ) +

ex.run2_caveat: The EM-calorimeter sampling (S) and constant (C) terms are detector-intrinsic quantities; no Run-2 13 TeV measurement re-derives them as a closed-form S,C-per-region table. The dedicated Run-2 fast-sim reference (AtlFast3, arXiv:2109.02551) parameterizes the EM shower energy directly with FastCaloSim V2 / FastCaloGAN (ML), and does NOT publish an S/sqrt(E) (+) C table per eta region, so it cannot supply these coefficients. The barrel/endcap values are therefore taken from the ATLAS EM barrel electron test-beam (physics/0608012, Eq.8: a=10.1+/-0.1%, b=0.17+/-0.04%) and the forward (FCal) values from the FCal electron test-beam (S~28.5%, constant term measured ~3-4%, ScienceDirect S0168900296008030 / FCal performance JINST 3 P02010). These intrinsic sampling/constant terms are unchanged between Run-1 and Run-2 (same LAr calorimeter), so the values are valid for Run-2 with the caveat that the effective in-situ constant term measured in data (Z->ee) is larger (~0.6-1.2% global, larger in the 1.37<|eta|<1.52 crack and high-|eta| endcap) than the local test-beam term.

v.checked: Re-read both cited sources cold. (1) arXiv:2301.02175 (PDF extracted locally): real CMS proceedings, "Jet Energy Scale and Resolution Measurements in CMS," Garvita Agarwal, ICHEP 2022; confirmed Run-2 Legacy, 138 fb-1, 13 TeV (2016-2018). Fig.6 caption verbatim: "JER versus pT for varying levels of PU, mu (left). JER data-to-simulation scale-factors vs. |eta_jet| ... (right). [10]". Left panel axis text confirms: "Anti-kT (R = 0.4), PF+CHS", "Run 2 Legacy, 138 fb-1 (13 TeV)", "0.0 <= eta < 0.5", y-axis JER 0-0.5, x-axis pt 30-2000 GeV, curves binned by PU (0<=mu<10 ... 40<=mu<50). So the source/figure (R=0.4, PF+CHS, barrel, Run-2) matches the locator. BUT the panel shows a family of PU-dependent JER curves with NO NSC fit overlaid and NO printed N/S/C values; text gives only "scale-factors are between 10-15%." (2) arXiv:1607.03663 (PDF extracted locally, pdfinfo Title): "Jet energy scale and resolution in the CMS experiment in pp collisions at 8 TeV" -- this is the 8 TeV JINST paper, NOT Run-2/13 TeV. Confirmed Eq.(38) is the NSC form sigma_pT/pT = sqrt(sgn(N)*N^2/pT^2 + S^2/pT + C^2). Confirmed Fig.38: constant term "0.0338 +/- 0.0002 for gluons, and 0.0406 +/- 0.0002 for quarks" -- but explicitly for Anti-kT R=0.5 (PF+CHS), |eta|<1.3, 8 TeV. Figs 36/37/38 are all global |eta|<1.3 for R=0.5/0.7; no per-eta-bin NSC fit table exists in the paper (grep for fitted N/S/C per eta returned nothing; only the 2 flavor C values).
v.corrections: Major fabrication: the entire 21-value per-eta-bin NSC table (N=3.4/3.6/4.2/4.0/3.6/3.0/3.5 GeV; S=0.83/0.85/0.90/0.95/1.05/1.20/1.10; C=0.043/0.046/0.050/0.045/0.040/0.050/0.055) for the 7 eta bins 0-0.5...3.0-5.0 appears NOWHERE in either cited source. Neither paper tabulates per-eta N, S, C fit parameters; the proceedings (2301.02175) gives no NSC fit at all, and the 8 TeV JINST paper gives only global |eta|<1.3 fits for R=0.5/0.7. These per-bin numbers and their unc_rel bands (0.05-0.25) are invented. Source-mismatch: C_gluon=0.0338/C_quark=0.0406 are real but for R=0.5, |eta|<1.3, 8 TeV -- not "barrel R=0.4" nor flavor-averaged ~0.043 (the averaging/extrapolation is the extractor's, not the source's). is_run2=true is half-wrong: the NSC parameterization and ALL N/S/C-related numbers derive from the 8 TeV (Run-1) JINST paper, not a Run-2 source; only the qualitative Fig.6 JER-vs-pt curve is Run-2 R=0.4. The "19% @30 / 10% @100 / 5% @1 TeV" read-off is approximate and unverifiable as a single value since Fig.6 shows a PU-binned family of curves, not one curve. Recommend rejecting the formula_terms wholesale and the delphes_fragment; only the source identification (R=0.4 PF+CHS Run-2 JER figure exists in 2301.02175, NSC form Eq.38 exists in 1607.03663) is sound.
